newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Prices seen weaker, market eyes spot expiry.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Prices seen weaker, market eyes spot expiry.

text.p: Japan's rubber futures markets are generally expected to drift lower for most of this week, with market attention focusing on Wednesday's spot expiry, traders said on Monday.

Several traders said that the spot April contract on TOCOM is likely to expire at lower levels, as few market players would be willing to accept deliveries due in part to the lower quality of the rubber in the exchange stocks.
The benchmark September contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 136.6 yen per kg, up marginally from 136.3 yen last Friday.
The benchmark September contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 136.5 yen per kg, also fractionally higher than last Friday's close of 136.3 yen.

Expectations that there would be a large number of deliveries at the spot expiry on Wednesday, while players may be unwilling to accept deliveries due to problems with quality, are likely to push down the spot contract's price at the expiry, traders said.
"We are watching how the spot April contract expires on Wednesday. If it goes out below 120 yen, the market will come under further pressure," one trader said.
"Despite emerging cautiousness that prices were too low after last week's sharp declines, fundamentally, bearish sentiment remains intact," he said.
Looming ample near-term supplies and continued price weakness in producing countries are seen as the main reasons for the bearishness, they said.
One analyst at a commodity broker said that initial support for the TOCOM benchmark September contract was seen at 135 yen, followed by 131.5 yen.

The analyst said lower prices in rubber-producing countries may prompt Japanese trade houses to purchase rubber there, leading to a further rise in Japanese rubber stocks, which have been on an upward trend.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at about 110 U.S. cents per kg on Monday, against 113 U.S. cents last Friday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end-users was quoted at 143 yen per kg on Monday, compared with 160 yen on April 14.
